title: #24 Writing and appearance settings
description:
**Roadmap #:** 24 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P2

### User problem
Default typography may not suit prolonged writing.

### Proposed behavior
Settings scene for editor font/size/spacing/width, system/light/dark appearance, explicit newline rendering policy; persist defaults tolerantly; apply to editor and preview without replacing document text.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Editor font/spacing/width and light/dark preferences.

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/WritingPreferences.swift; Sources/Silkweb/SettingsView.swift; style adapters.

### Constraints
Backward-compatible preference JSON.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.24 Writing and appearance settings
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§4 editor typography defaults, §6: Settings… ⌘,, Bigger/Smaller/Actual Size ⌘+/⌘−/⌘0). This feeds the `EditorStyle` introduced in 1.5 and the preview CSS variables from 1.18.

### Settings window (SwiftUI `Settings` scene)
A `TabView` with toolbar-style tabs: **Editor** (`textformat`), **Preview** (`eye`), **Appearance** (`circle.lefthalf.filled`). Width 500pt, height fits content. Use `Form` with `.formStyle(.grouped)`. Changes apply **live**. There's no Apply/OK. Each tab ends with a trailing **Restore Defaults** button (restores that tab only).

**Editor tab**
| Label | Control | Default / range |
|---|---|---|
| Font | Picker: System, Serif (New York), Monospaced (SF Mono), Custom… | System |
| Custom… | opens `NSFontPanel`; the picker then shows the chosen family name | — |
| Size | numeric field + stepper, "pt" suffix | 15 (10–32) |
| Line height | Picker: 1.2, 1.35, 1.5, 1.75, 2.0 | 1.5 |
| Text width | Picker: Narrow (600 pt), Medium (720 pt), Wide (900 pt), Full Width | Medium |
| Indent with | Picker: 2 Spaces, 4 Spaces, Tab | 4 Spaces |
| Spelling | Toggle "Check spelling while typing" | on |
| Substitutions | Toggle "Use smart quotes and dashes" | off |
Below the table: a **Sample** box, 80pt tall, rendered with the current editor style and 1.12 styling: "## A heading" + "Some **bold** text and `code`." This is the live preview of the settings. 1.27 adds a **Writing Modes** section to this tab.

**Preview tab**
| Label | Control | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Font | Picker: System, Serif (New York) | System |
| Size | stepper | 16 (12–24) |
| Line breaks | Radio group: "Join lines in a paragraph (standard Markdown)" / "Treat every line break as a new line" | Join |

**Appearance tab**
- "Appearance": segmented control **System | Light | Dark**, default System. Sets `NSApp.appearance`; the editor, preview and export dialogs follow.
- Static caption: "Silkweb uses your system accent color. Change it in System Settings › Appearance." No accent picker, per the design system.

### Shortcuts tied to settings
**View ▸ Bigger ⌘+, Smaller ⌘−, Actual Size ⌘0** change the editor size in 1pt steps within range. This is a temporary per-window zoom on top of the Settings size. **Actual Size** returns to the Settings value, and the zoom doesn't rewrite the preference. *(Orchestrator: confirm per-window temporary zoom.)*

### Behavior
- Applying a style never replaces text storage (keep the selection, scroll and undo). Re-layout only.
- Preview updates via CSS variables (`--sw-font-size`, `--sw-font-family`) injected without a full re-render.
- Out-of-range values in older or edited preference files clamp to the nearest bound. Unknown fonts fall back to System with no alert.

### Accessibility
Every control has a visible label (Form rows). The font picker announces the family. The sample box is labeled "Editor sample text". Dynamic adjustments respect Reduce Motion (no animated re-layout).

### Out of scope
Custom themes and CSS, separate UI font, per-library settings, editor color customization, keyboard shortcut customization.

title: #25 Keyboard, accessibility completion and document statistics
description:
**Roadmap #:** 25 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P2

### User problem
Frequent actions need consistent keyboard access, accessibility labels, and writing feedback.

### Proposed behavior
Complete menu validation and shortcuts across shipped surfaces; focus traversal and accessible labels; debounced word/character counts for document and selection.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Menus, editor focus, word/selection counts.

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/DocumentStatistics.swift; Sources/Silkweb/AppCommands.swift; existing workspace views.

### Constraints
Integration polish only—basic accessibility must not wait for this ticket on prior UI.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.25 Keyboard, accessibility completion and document statistics
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§5.6 Status Bar, §6 shortcut map, §7 accessibility baseline). This ticket **audits** the shipped app against §6 and §7 and fixes gaps. It also introduces the Status Bar and word counts.

### Status Bar (new shared component)
- A 24pt strip at the bottom of the detail column, `.bar` material, top hairline `separatorColor`, 12pt horizontal padding, `.caption` secondary monospaced digits.
- **Leading:** "1,204 words · 6,830 characters". With a non-empty selection: "38 of 1,204 words · 212 of 6,830 characters".
- **Trailing:** reserved for the Focus/Typewriter chip (1.27) and transient progress (1.15 "Adding 3 files…").
- **View ▸ Show Status Bar ⌘/** (the title flips to Hide). On by default, persisted. It stays visible in Preview-only mode, since counts still apply.
- Click on the counts: a popover with Words, Characters, Characters (no spaces), Paragraphs and Reading time ("about 5 min", 230 wpm).

### Count definitions (Core `DocumentStatistics`, unit-tested)
- **Words:** Unicode word segmentation of the source text. Each CJK ideograph, kana run character or Hangul syllable block counts as one word. Markdown punctuation-only tokens (`#`, `-`, `*`, `|`, `>`, fences) aren't words. URLs inside `(…)` of links/images aren't counted. *(Orchestrator: confirm counting source text minus markup, rather than rendered text.)*
- **Characters:** grapheme clusters, including spaces and excluding line breaks.
- Debounce 300 ms after the last edit. Documents over 50k characters compute off-main. The selection count updates on selection change with the same debounce.

### Shortcut and menu audit (deliverable checklist)
1. Every command in §6 exists with exactly that equivalent. No duplicates (write a unit test over a Core `CommandCatalog` table if commands are declared there).
2. **Menu validation by focus:** Format and Find items need an editable editor focus. Rename, Move to Trash and Move To… need sidebar or list focus with a valid selection. Export, Print and Tags need one document. Disabled items stay visible.
3. Context-menu titles match the menu bar exactly ("Move to Trash", "Reveal in Finder").
4. Focus loop: Tab / ⇧Tab sidebar → list → editor → inspector. Go ▸ ⌥⌘1/2/3 work from anywhere, including from the find bar and banners.

### Accessibility audit (each surface)
- Sidebar row: "<name>, folder, 8 documents". List row (one element): "<title>, modified <date>[, in <path>][, tags: a, b]".
- All icon-only toolbar buttons: label + `.help` in menu wording. Segmented editor modes are labeled.
- Banners, move/trash results and import completion post `NSAccessibility` announcements.
- Drag alternatives: Move To… (1.7), Image… (1.15).
- Reduce Motion: no spring-load or expand animations; Typewriter scroll is instant.
- Increase Contrast: no custom colors means system handling applies. Verify no text uses `quaternaryLabelColor`.
- Write static or structural tests where possible (accessibility labels defined in one place, e.g. `AccessibilityLabels.swift`, unit-tested for non-empty strings).

### Out of scope
Custom shortcut editing, VoiceOver rotor customizations, goals or targets for word counts, the stats history.
acceptance_criteria:

- [ ] `./scripts/build.sh test` passes with new XCTest coverage for AppCommands; existing workspace views. logic
- [ ] Word and character counts update debounced and handle Unicode/CJK per tests
- [ ] Menu commands validate enabled state based on focus context
- [ ] Accessibility labels present on primary sidebar, list, and editor controls (static/structure tests where applicable)

title: #26 Document tabs and session restore
description:
**Scope:** L · **Priority:** P2 · **Product-owner request (2026-10-01)**

### User problem
The three-pane shell (#4) and single-document editor (#5) cannot keep multiple notes open, reuse a preview slot, or restore the last working set after quit—unlike MWeb’s tabbed editor workflow (`research.md` **Tabs/session**).

### Proposed behavior
- **Tab bar** in the editor pane of the main window: each tab binds one library document (stable ID from #1) with its own dirty buffer via `DocumentSession` / save coordinator (#3, #5).
- **Preview vs pinned:** one replaceable *preview* tab; selecting a document in the list opens it there unless that document is already open in another tab. First edit or double-click *fixes* the tab (pinned); pinned tabs persist across list selections until closed.
- **Tab chrome:** reorder (drag), close, **Close Others**, **Close Tabs to the Right**; **Cmd-W** closes the active tab (not the window when tabs remain—align with standard Mac tab semantics).
- **Navigation:** **Ctrl-Tab** and **Cmd-Shift-]** activate next tab (document shortcut collision matrix in #25; do not steal Cmd-R preview toggle, Cmd-O / Cmd-Shift-O open paths from #20, or find/replace keys from #13).
- **Session restore:** on launch, restore open tabs (pinned + preview state), active tab, and selected folder from versioned library/window metadata; decode tolerantly; drop entries whose files are missing; when a file was moved externally, rebind tab to the same stable document ID via library reconcile (#11) / move IDs (#7) when possible.
- **Moves:** when #7 moves or renames a document, open tabs follow the file path without orphan buffers.
- **Quit/close:** save coordinator flushes every dirty tab before tab close, window close, and app termination.

### MWeb / competitor reference
`research.md` **Tabs/session** (H/L2): replaceable preview tab; editing or double-click makes tab fixed; reorder/close subsets; reopen last session.

### Likely files
Sources/Silkweb/EditorTabBar.swift, TabbedEditorPane.swift, LibraryWorkspace.swift (list → tab routing), DocumentSession.swift, AppCommands.swift; Sources/SilkwebCore/WindowSessionMetadata.swift (or extend LibraryMetadata.swift) with tolerant Codable + tests in Tests/SilkwebCoreTests/WindowSessionMetadataTests.swift.

### Constraints
- Repo today is skeleton-only (`SilkwebApp.swift` placeholder; no tab or shortcut code yet)—implement on top of #4/#5 deliverables.
- Follow #5 autosave/debounce and flush-before-close; follow #7 move/link semantics for open documents.
- Session JSON must version and default missing keys; never block launch on stale session data.
- No per-keystroke library rescan (AGENTS.md performance rules).
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.26 Document tabs and session restore
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§3 detail column, §4 `.bar` material, §6: ⌘T, ⌘W, ⇧⌘W, ⌃⇥ / ⇧⌘], ⌃⇧⇥ / ⇧⌘[, ⌥⌘W). Tabs are **inside the detail column** of the one library window. They're not `NSWindow` tabs, which would create separate windows with separate sidebars.

### Tab bar
- Sits directly under the window toolbar, above any Editor Banner and the find bar. 28pt tall, `.bar` material, bottom hairline `separatorColor`.
- **Shown when 2 or more tabs are open.** With a single tab (or none) it's hidden, so a single-document workflow looks identical to before (Safari-like). *(Orchestrator: confirm; alternative is "always show".)*
- Tabs share width equally, min 110pt, max 220pt. Beyond the available width the bar scrolls horizontally, with an overflow `chevron.down` menu at the trailing edge listing all tabs.
- **Tab anatomy:** a centered `.callout` title (document name, middle-truncated) and a 16pt close button on the leading side. The close button appears on hover and on the active tab. When the document is dirty, a `•` replaces the ✕ until hovered (Xcode/Safari convention).
- **Active tab:** `controlBackgroundColor` fill and primary text. **Inactive:** no fill and secondary text. Hover adds a subtle `quaternarySystemFill`.
- **Preview tab:** title in *italic* with tooltip "Preview — edit or double-click to keep this tab open". Only one preview tab exists at a time.
```
| ✕ plan for q3 | • outline | *meeting notes* |          ⌄ |
   active          dirty        preview (italic)
```

### Behavior
- **List selection** (single click, arrow keys, Search or Quick Open Return): if the document is already open in any tab, activate it. Otherwise, load it into the preview tab, creating one if needed and placing it right of the active tab.
- **Pinning:** the first edit, a double-click on the list row, a double-click on the tab, or the tab context item **Keep Open** turns the preview tab into a normal tab (title no longer italic).
- **⌘T / File ▸ Open in New Tab** (and ⌘Return in Quick Open, the list context menu's "Open in New Tab") opens the selection as a pinned tab.
- **Reorder** by dragging within the bar; a 2pt accent insertion indicator shows the gap. Dragging out of the window or between windows is out of scope.
- **Close:** ⌘W closes the active tab, then activates the tab to its **right**, else the left. With no tabs, ⌘W closes the window. ⇧⌘W always closes the window. Middle-click closes a tab.
- **Tab context menu:** Close Tab (⌘W) · Close Other Tabs (⌥⌘W) · Close Tabs to the Right · — · Keep Open (preview tab only) · Reveal in Library (selects in the sidebar and list) · Reveal in Finder.
- **Cycling:** Window ▸ Show Next Tab ⌃⇥ / ⇧⌘], Show Previous Tab ⌃⇧⇥ / ⇧⌘[ (wraps). ⌘1–9 are intentionally not tab selectors (§6).
- **Sync:** activating a tab selects its folder in the sidebar and its row in the list, unless a search is active (then only the editor changes).

### Saving
Closing a tab flushes its save. If the save fails, the tab stays open, becomes active, and shows the 1.5 banner. With tabs, switching documents no longer blocks on save failures: each tab keeps its own buffer, undo stack, caret and scroll.
Quit or window close flushes all tabs. Failures use the 1.5 quit alert.

### Session restore (silent)
Restore the open tabs (order, pinned/preview), active tab, caret and scroll per tab, selected folder, and view mode. Missing documents are dropped silently. Moved documents rebind by ID (1.7/1.11). Stale session data never blocks launch or shows an alert.

### Accessibility
The tab bar is an `AXTabGroup`. Tabs are radio-button-like with the label "<name>[, edited][, preview]". Close buttons are labeled "Close <name>". All tab commands are in the Window menu, so the mouse is never required.

### Out of scope
Multiple windows or libraries, tab tear-off, split editor groups, pinned/sticky tab icons, reopening closed tabs (⇧⌘T reserved for later).

title: #27 Focus and typewriter writing modes
description:
**Scope:** M · **Priority:** P2 · **Product-owner request (2026-10-01)**

### User problem
Long-form writing in the source editor lacks distraction-reducing view modes MWeb exposes in preferences (`research.md` **Focus/typewriter**): a focus dimming mode and typewriter-style vertical caret anchoring.

### Proposed behavior
- **View menu** toggles (per window, checkable): **Focus Mode** and **Typewriter Mode**; states persist in user preferences and restore per window where applicable.
- **Focus:** dim all text except the active **paragraph** (default) or **sentence**—granularity is a setting added to the writing preferences model alongside #24 fields.
- **Typewriter:** keep the caret line at a fixed vertical position (default: vertical center of the visible editor) while typing/scrolling; works together with Focus.
- **Rendering:** dimming composes with incremental Markdown styling attributes from #12 (no full-buffer syntax pass); update only visible range / affected paragraphs on caret or edit notifications—no per-keystroke whole-document work (AGENTS.md).
- **Settings UI:** extend the #24 settings scene with Focus granularity and typewriter vertical anchor (and any threshold slider if needed); defaults documented and tolerant on decode.

### MWeb / competitor reference
`research.md` **Focus/typewriter** (L2): focus toggle and typewriter scrolling-threshold preference; exact MWeb dimming curve unverified—match readable contrast, not pixel parity.

### Likely files
Sources/Silkweb/MarkdownTextView.swift (visible-range attribute updates, scroll anchoring), FocusTypewriterController.swift; Sources/SilkwebCore/WritingPreferences.swift (new keys); Sources/Silkweb/SettingsView.swift (additional rows); AppCommands.swift (View menu); Tests/SilkwebCoreTests/WritingPreferencesTests.swift (defaults/bounds).

### Constraints
- Depends on #12 so formatting attributes and IME/undo grouping remain correct when dimming.
- Depends on #24 for preference persistence and settings shell—this ticket adds keys + UI rows rather than expanding #24’s original acceptance scope.
- Keyboard shortcuts for toggles defer to #25 integration pass except where needed for basic menu validation; do not collide with tab shortcuts from the tabs ticket.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.27 Focus and typewriter writing modes
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§4 semantic colors, §5.6 Status Bar, §6: Focus Mode ⌃⇧⌘F, Typewriter Mode ⌃⇧⌘T). This builds on 1.12 styling, 1.24 settings, and the 1.25 status bar.

### Entry points
- **View ▸ Focus Mode ⌃⇧⌘F** and **View ▸ Typewriter Mode ⌃⇧⌘T**: checkmark items in their own group after the editor-mode items (Show Preview / Split / Outline). They're enabled when the editor is visible (Editor or Split mode) and disabled in Preview-only mode, where the state is kept.
- There are **no toolbar buttons**, to keep chrome minimal. While either mode is on, the trailing side of the Status Bar shows a borderless chip: "Focus", "Typewriter" or "Focus · Typewriter". It's `.caption`, accent-colored, and clicking it opens a menu with both toggles. This is the visible way out of the mode.
- The state is per window and persisted. New windows start with the last-used state.

### Focus Mode visuals
- Non-active text is dimmed by applying **temporary attributes** (`NSLayoutManager.addTemporaryAttribute(.foregroundColor)`) set to the run's existing color at about 30% opacity (blend toward `textBackgroundColor`). This never touches text storage, undo or 1.12 attributes. Markers already tertiary drop proportionally.
- **Active region**, per setting: **Paragraph** (default; a blank-line-delimited block, so a list item or a fenced code block counts as one unit) or **Sentence** (`enumerateSubstrings(.bySentences)` within the paragraph). A selection spanning several regions activates all of them.
- Updates on selection change, coalesced once per run loop, for the visible glyph range plus one screen of overscan only. No animation: the change is instantaneous, which avoids flicker while typing.
- It works in light and dark mode automatically because opacity is relative to the semantic colors.
```
GOOD                                   BAD
 dim  The previous paragraph…           Blurring or hiding text: unreadable
 FULL The one I'm typing in now|        Dimming to <20%: lost context, fails contrast
 dim  The next paragraph…               Dimming headings differently: inconsistent
```

### Typewriter Mode behavior
- Keeps the **caret line** at the anchor: Upper Third (33%), **Middle (50%, default)** or Lower Third (66%) of the visible editor height.
- Re-anchors on text input and keyboard caret movement only. Mouse or trackpad scrolling is free and doesn't fight the user, and a mouse click doesn't jump the view; the next keystroke re-anchors.
- Scrolling is instant (no animation; this also satisfies Reduce Motion). The 1.5 bottom inset already lets the last line reach the anchor. Add an equivalent top inset when on, so the first line can too.
- Find (1.13) and Outline (1.18) jumps land at the anchor instead of the top third.

### Settings (1.24 Editor tab, new section "Writing Modes")
| Label | Control | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Focus highlights | Segmented: Paragraph · Sentence | Paragraph |
| Typewriter position | Picker: Upper Third · Middle · Lower Third | Middle |

### Accessibility
Dimming is visual only: VoiceOver reads all text normally, and the menu items report their checked state. With Increase Contrast enabled, raise dim opacity to 55%. Focus and Typewriter don't change keyboard behavior.

### Out of scope
Full-screen "distraction-free" chrome hiding (use the system ⌃⌘F full screen plus the sidebar toggle), line-level or custom dim levels, typewriter sound effects.

title: Crash (stack overflow) when opening a document in the editor
description:
Reported by the product owner: opening a file in a library quits the app immediately.

Crash report ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/Silkweb-2026-10-01-100728.ips: EXC_BAD_ACCESS / SIGSEGV KERN_PROTECTION_FAILURE on the main thread = stack overflow from infinite recursion:
PlainMarkdownTextView.setFrameSize (MarkdownTextView.swift:128) -> layoutEditor() -> textContainer.containerSize = ... (:134) / textContainerInset = ... (:135) -> NSTextContainer setSize / NSTextView setTextContainerInset -> NSLayoutManager textContainerChangedGeometry -> view resized -> setFrameSize -> layoutEditor -> ... forever.

Root cause: layoutEditor() mutates geometry that itself resizes the text view, and it is invoked from setFrameSize unconditionally. Fix direction (engineer decides): compute layout from the scroll view's content size, not the text view frame; only assign containerSize/textContainerInset/minSize/contentInsets when the value actually changes; add a re-entrancy guard; consider driving it from the scroll view's frame-change notification (NSView.frameDidChangeNotification on the clip view) instead of overriding setFrameSize; make sure widthTracksTextView/heightTracksTextView settings don't fight the manual container size.

Regression test is REQUIRED because QA cannot launch the GUI: add an app-level test target (e.g. testTarget SilkwebAppTests depending on the Silkweb executable target, using @testable import) that builds the real editor view hierarchy offscreen (NSScrollView + the editor text view, no window shown, or an NSWindow that is never ordered front), loads a multi-paragraph document, and resizes it across a sweep of widths/heights (tiny, narrower than insets, typical, very wide, maximumWidth boundary) without recursion. Keep it runnable via ./scripts/build.sh test inside the sandbox. Likely files: Sources/Silkweb/MarkdownTextView.swift, Package.swift, Tests/SilkwebAppTests/.

title: #3 Atomic document save coordinator
description:
**Roadmap #:** 3 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Interrupted or failed saves must not lose user writing.

### Proposed behavior
Serialized per-document writes with temp-file replace, revision token, recoverable draft on failure; dirty state clears only on successful commit.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Editable local notes and recovery-oriented workflow (implementation details U).

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/DocumentStore.swift, SaveCoordinator.swift; Tests/SilkwebCoreTests/SaveCoordinatorTests.swift with injected filesystem failures.

### Constraints
Atomic write temp + replace; never lose text on failure paths.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.3 Atomic save coordinator (Core-only)
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§5.2 Editor Banner). There is no UI here. 1.5 maps these states to UI, so expose them as an observable per-document state, not strings.

**Save state enum** (what the UI shows):
| State | UI in 1.5 |
|---|---|
| `clean` | nothing; window close button has no dirty dot |
| `dirty` (edited, save pending) | close-button dirty dot (`isDocumentEdited`) |
| `saving` | nothing new (avoid flicker); dot remains |
| `failed(error, attempt)` | Editor Banner (see below) and the dot remains |
| `conflict(diskRevision)` | handed to 1.11's conflict banner |

Never show a spinner for routine saves.

**Error copy** (`LocalizedError`), used in the banner as "Silkweb couldn’t save “<name>”." plus a reason line:
- Disk full: "There isn’t enough space on the disk."
- Permission: "You don’t have permission to write to “<folder>”."
- Volume gone: "The disk containing this library is no longer available."
- File vanished during save: route to 1.11 (external delete), not a generic error.
- Other: underlying `localizedDescription`.

Recovery is always implied, so the reason line ends with: "Your text is safe in this window."

**Recovery draft:** when a save fails, or at quit with unsaved text, write a draft under Application Support (not inside the library). Expose `pendingRecoveryDrafts()` so the app can show on next launch: "Silkweb recovered unsaved changes to 2 documents." with buttons "Review…" and "Later". The review UI is a follow-up. For v1, at minimum open each recovered draft in the editor as dirty.

**Revision token:** used by 1.11 to detect "changed on disk since load". No UI.

**Out of scope:** banners/alerts themselves (1.5), conflict UI (1.11).

title: Resizing the document list column also resizes the folder sidebar
description:
Reported by the product owner: dragging the divider between the document list and the editor also changes the width of the folder sidebar.

Expected (standard Mac three-pane behavior, e.g. Mail/Notes): each divider resizes only its two neighbouring panes. Dragging the list|editor divider changes the list and editor widths and leaves the folder sidebar width unchanged; dragging the sidebar|list divider changes sidebar and list. Resizing the WINDOW gives/takes space from the editor first; the sidebar and list keep their widths until they would violate the editor minimum. Widths persist across relaunch (per window/library is fine). Collapsing/showing the sidebar (toolbar button, Ctrl-Cmd-S) must keep working.

Current code: Sources/Silkweb/LibraryWorkspace.swift:255 NavigationSplitView(columnVisibility:) with navigationSplitViewColumnWidth on sidebar (:268, 180/220/320), content (DocumentList.swift:54, 240/300/480) and detail (DocumentList.swift:112, min 420/ideal 680). SwiftUI's NavigationSplitView redistributes column widths itself. Engineer: first try to fix within NavigationSplitView (e.g. column width constraints); if it can't be made to hold the sidebar width, host the three panes in an AppKit NSSplitViewController (sidebar item via NSSplitViewItem(sidebarWithViewController:), content item, detail item) with holding priorities sidebar > list > editor and autosaveName for persistence, keeping the SwiftUI views as NSHostingController children. Do not regress keyboard pane focus (Opt-Cmd-1/2/3), the toolbar, or the window title/subtitle.

GUI regression rule (AGENTS.md) applies: add an offscreen test in Tests/SilkwebAppTests that builds the real split layout, drags/sets the list|editor divider position and asserts the sidebar width is unchanged, and resizes the window asserting the editor absorbs the change.

title: Document list rows only respond to clicks on part of the row
description:
Reported by the product owner: clicking a document in the list only selects it when clicking a specific spot; clicks elsewhere in the row do nothing.

Root cause (DocumentList.swift, DocumentRow as of 3893e7c):
1. The row's VStack has no .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading) and no .contentShape(Rectangle()), so only the pixels covered by text are hit-testable; empty space to the right of a short title and the gap between the two lines don't select.
2. The slow-click-to-rename is implemented as .simultaneousGesture(TapGesture()) on the title Text inside a List row. On macOS, gestures on List row content compete with the table's own mouse-down selection handling and can swallow/delay selection.

Expected: a click ANYWHERE in the row rectangle (full width, full height incl. padding) selects the document immediately, exactly like Finder/Mail; Cmd-click and Shift-click multi-select still work; slow-click on the already-selected single row (0.5–1.5 s) still starts rename; double-click does not rename; drag (from silkweb-1.7) still starts from anywhere on the row. Implement slow-click without attaching a tap gesture that competes with selection — e.g. detect it from selection changes + a click-timestamp in the selection binding, or an NSEvent-based approach — engineer decides. Also verify the folder sidebar (NSOutlineView) rows are fully clickable.

GUI regression rule (AGENTS.md) applies: add an offscreen test in Tests/SilkwebAppTests that hosts the real DocumentList, and asserts hit-testing at several points across a row (left edge, title, right empty area, between lines, bottom padding) resolves to that row / selects it. If true click simulation isn't feasible offscreen, assert the row's hit-test frame equals the full row bounds and unit-test the slow-click timing logic separately.

title: Moves/undo fail when Finder adds .DS_Store; folder links lose trailing slash
description:
Carryovers from silkweb-1.7 QA (qa_silkweb-1.7_2.md), judged must-fix by the orchestrator:

1. A stray .DS_Store (or any other new hidden/ignored file the scanner already excludes) appearing in an affected folder between preflight and execute, or between move and undo, makes execute/undo fail with 'items have changed'. title: Regression: clicking a document in the list no longer selects it at all
description:
Reported by the product owner on build 941eff0: no document in the list can be selected by clicking anywhere. Earlier build 3893e7c (before silkweb-1.7 and silkweb-1.32) selected rows when clicking on text. silkweb-1.32 QA passed on code review + hit-test geometry only; no test ever delivered a real mouse click to the list, so this regression was invisible to the pipeline.

Prime suspect (orchestrator analysis of DocumentList.swift @ 941eff0): silkweb-1.7 attached SwiftUI .onDrag { … } preview: { … } to every List row, and silkweb-1.32 then made the row's interaction shape the full rectangle (.contentShape([.interaction, .dragPreview], Rectangle())). On macOS, a SwiftUI drag gesture on List row content intercepts mouse-down for the whole interaction shape, so NSTableView never receives the click and selection never changes. The DocumentRowClickObserver (hitTest -> nil, local NSEvent monitor that returns every event) looks benign but must be ruled out too.

Fix direction: drag documents with the List's native row drag hook instead of a content gesture — on macOS use the row modifier .itemProvider { … } (NSTableView-backed, keeps selection and multi-select) or an AppKit-level drag source; keep the full-row hit area; keep the slow-click observer only if proven not to interfere. Do NOT regress silkweb-1.7 drag/drop, Move To…, or silkweb-1.32 full-row clicking and slow-click rename.

REQUIRED regression test (AGENTS.md GUI rule, and the missing piece last time): an offscreen test in Tests/SilkwebAppTests that hosts the real DocumentList inside an NSWindow (not ordered front), synthesizes real NSEvent leftMouseDown/leftMouseUp events via window.sendEvent at several points of a row (title, empty right area, between lines), and asserts workspace.session.selectedDocuments changes to that row. Also Cmd-click adds a second row. If synthesized events can't drive SwiftUI List offscreen, say so explicitly in the report and provide the closest real-event test possible (e.g. driving the underlying NSTableView with sendEvent). The orchestrator will verify the test FAILS against 941eff0.

title: Library isn't reopened after a rebuild/update ('Can't Open Library — choose your library folder again')
description:
Reported by the product owner (screenshot): launching a new build shows 'Can't Open Library — Choose your library folder again to restore access.' every time.

Root cause (orchestrator): LibraryWorkspace stores the library location as a SECURITY-SCOPED bookmark (bookmarkData(options: [.withSecurityScope]) at LibraryWorkspace.swift:197; URL(resolvingBookmarkData:options:[.withSecurityScope]) at :107). Security-scoped bookmarks are bound to the app's code signature, and scripts/bundle_app.sh produces an ad-hoc-signed app whose code identity changes on every build (codesign identifier 'Silkweb-<cdhash>'), so each rebuild — and any future update — can't resolve the previous build's bookmark.

Fix: the app is not App-Sandboxed, so a security scope isn't needed. (1) Save a regular bookmark (no .withSecurityScope; e.g. [] or .minimalBookmark) PLUS the standardized path as a fallback; on launch resolve the bookmark without security scope, fall back to the saved path if resolution fails but the folder exists, refresh the stored bookmark when stale, and only show the error when the folder truly can't be found/read ('Library Not Found' / 'Can't Open Library'). (2) Migrate: an existing security-scoped bookmark in UserDefaults 'libraryBookmark' must still be tried, then replaced with the new format; users must not have to re-choose the folder more than once. (3) In scripts/bundle_app.sh, codesign ad-hoc with a stable identifier (codesign --force -s - -i com.silkweb.app build/Silkweb.app) so the code identity is consistent across builds. Keep startAccessingSecurityScopedResource calls harmless (call only when a scoped URL was actually resolved), so a future sandboxed build can opt back in. Put the resolve/fallback/migration decision logic in SilkwebCore and unit-test it.

- [x] `./scripts/build.sh test` passes with new XCTest coverage for library-location restore: regular bookmark resolves; unresolvable bookmark falls back to an existing saved path; stale bookmark is refreshed; legacy security-scoped bookmark data is tried then migrated; missing folder -> Library Not Found; unreadable folder -> Can't Open Library
- [x] Rebuilding the app (new binary) and relaunching reopens the same library without asking (verified by rebuilding twice in a test harness or by orchestrator/owner check)
- [x] scripts/bundle_app.sh signs with a stable identifier; `codesign -dv build/Silkweb.app` shows Identifier=com.silkweb.app
- [x] Choosing a folder still works and persists the new format

title: Image paste/drop can silently do nothing right after launch
description: From silkweb-1.15 QA (advisory, judged must-fix): MarkdownTextView.swift (~line 90) resolves the current document's ID only when the document URL or library root changes. If the library snapshot isn't loaded yet at that moment (e.g. right after launch / restore), documentID stays nil and image paste/drop/Format > Image… silently does nothing until the user reselects the document. Fix: resolve the document ID lazily at insertion time (or re-resolve when the snapshot/revision changes); if it still can't be resolved, show the existing error banner instead of failing silently. Also: when the pasteboard has both a file URL/image and its filename as text (copying an image in Finder), prefer the image/file over the text.

title: Idle redraw loop: placeholder and Search Library results blink continuously
description:
Reported by the product owner on build 47cda03: (1) opening a new/empty document, the "Start writing…" placeholder flickers/blinks continuously; (2) the same idle blinking appears in **Search Library** results (⇧⌘F, silkweb-1.20) — **not** in in-document Find (⌘F, silkweb-1.13).

**Suggested build order (this batch):** silkweb-1.42 → **1.40 → 1.39 → 1.44 → 1.43 → 1.41** (this ticket after 1.40).

**Boundary vs silkweb-1.40:** **1.40 must land first** (preview read-access fix + suspend preview rendering when the preview pane is hidden). **This ticket owns remaining idle stability** — editor placeholder drawing, Search Library results list, and any shared workspace `@Observable`/SwiftUI publish loops that still repaint UI while idle. Do not re-implement the preview URL scheme here.

**Boundary vs silkweb-1.20 / silkweb-1.19:** Search ranking, indexing, and panel layout stay in 1.19/1.20; this ticket only stops **idle** re-query/rebuild/redraw of an unchanged Search Library query and keeps result rows visually steady.

**Boundary vs silkweb-1.18:** Functional preview/outline behavior stays in 1.18/1.40; this is a regression fix on idle redraw, not preview feature work.

**Placeholder:** drawn in `PlainMarkdownTextView.draw(_:)` (`MarkdownTextView.swift:275-282`), so it flickers whenever the view is repeatedly redrawn/cleared. Hypotheses (prove which): (a) a continuous redraw loop — silkweb-1.18 QA noted the preview re-renders every 250 ms even in Editor-only mode (`PreviewCoordinator.schedule` / `DocumentPanes`), and each publish triggers SwiftUI `updateNSView` paths that set `text.needsDisplay = true` (`MarkdownTextView.swift` ~112/~147), repainting the whole editor; (b) the blinking insertion point's redraw rect clears part of the placeholder each blink (caret sits at `textContainerOrigin`, where the placeholder starts); (c) a layer-backed redraw that clears before drawing; (d) for Search Library — the 150 ms search debounce re-running an unchanged query and rebuilding results, or the same workspace publish loop rebuilding the list column.

Fix direction: after 1.40's preview idle fix, stop any remaining idle re-render/publish loops affecting the editor and Search Library; draw the placeholder robustly (e.g. a non-editable `NSTextField`/label overlay hidden when text is non-empty, or draw it only in `drawBackground` so caret redraws don't clear it). Keep the 1.18 preview behavior (debounced latest-result-only rendering when the preview pane is visible) and 1.20 search behavior when the query **changes**. Must not regress silkweb-1.29 layout recursion fix.

**REQUIRED test (GUI rule):** offscreen app test hosting the real editor (+ preview in each mode: editor-only, split, preview-only) with an empty document, run the main run loop ~1.5 s idle, and assert (1) the preview renderer is not invoked while idle/hidden and (2) the editor's draw count stays bounded (only caret-blink sized redraws or zero full redraws). Extend the same harness (or a sibling test) for Search Library open with a fixed query and populated results: over ~1.5 s idle assert the search index/query is not re-run and the results list is not rebuilt/redrawn repeatedly. Orchestrator will check the test fails on 47cda03.

**Snapshot (silkweb-1.42):** scenarios `empty-document` and `search-results` should show steady UI in light/dark PNGs after fix (QA views `empty-document-light/dark.png` and `search-results-light/dark.png`).
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.39 Stable "Start writing…" placeholder
Foundation: `docs/design-system.md` §4 (editor typography, semantic colors). This is a bug fix, so there's no new UI. The notes pin down how the placeholder should look and behave once it's stable.

### Look (unchanged from today, just steady)
- Copy: **"Start writing…"** with a real ellipsis character (…), not three dots. Sentence case, no trailing period.
- Font: the editor's current body font and size, so it follows 1.24 Bigger/Smaller (⌘+ / ⌘−). Paragraph style is the editor's default (1.5× line height). Color: `tertiaryLabelColor`, so light and dark come free.
- Position: the first line's origin (`textContainerOrigin`, honoring the 24pt top inset and the centered 720pt column). The placeholder's **baseline must match the baseline of the first typed character**, so typing replaces it in place with no 1–2pt jump. The baseline can drift if the text is drawn with `draw(at:)` and no paragraph style. Use the same attributes as `typingAttributes`, with only the color changed.
- The caret blinks at the start of the placeholder. The caret blinks; the placeholder never does. A caret redraw must not erase any placeholder pixels.

### States
| State | Placeholder |
|---|---|
| Empty, editable, focused or not | Shown, steady |
| First keystroke, including IME marked text (e.g. Japanese composition) and paste | Hidden immediately, in the same frame. No fade |
| User deletes all text | Shown again immediately |
| Empty read-only document (§5.2 read-only banner visible) | **Not shown.** Inviting typing would be misleading |
| Find bar open on an empty doc | Shown; it doesn't move |
| Focus/Typewriter Mode (1.27) | Shown at full tertiary color, not dimmed |

No animation at all, so Reduce Motion needs no special handling.

### Accessibility
The placeholder is not text content. VoiceOver must not read it as the document's value. Expose it as the text view's `accessibilityPlaceholderValue` ("Start writing…"), so VoiceOver says "Start writing…, text area, empty".

### Verification surface
Snapshot scenario `empty-document` (1.42), light and dark: the placeholder sits in tertiary gray at the top-left of the centered column, aligned with the 40pt-inset text column. It must not be clipped or doubled, and no part of it may be missing.

### Out of scope
Changing the copy, per-folder placeholder text, or showing the placeholder in Preview (Preview's empty state stays "Nothing to preview" from 1.18).

### Search Library results (steady rows)
- Applies only while Search Library is open with a **fixed** query and stable result set (orchestrator owner report).
- Result rows, match highlights, and path snippets must not flicker or rebuild visually while idle; scrolling and changing the query behave as in silkweb-1.20.
- Snapshot `search-results`: rows for query "coffee" remain fully visible with highlights, not partially erased between frames.

### Search Library — steady rendering
This expands "steady rows" above. It is shared with Quick Open (1.19), which uses the same `LibrarySearch` and `SearchRequestIdentity` and follows the same rules. Layout, copy and ranking stay as in 1.20.

**Idle (query unchanged):** nothing on screen changes. That covers rows, highlights, the "N results" caption, scroll position and selection. A `revision` bump from an index state or reconcile event re-runs the query only if the index content actually changed. Results are assigned only when the hit list differs (compare IDs and snippets), so `onChange(of: results)` doesn't fire.

**Typing:** keep the 150 ms debounce. Earlier results stay visible and readable until the new results arrive, then swap in a single frame. Never clear the list or show an empty state in between, and never fade. Rows whose IDs survive keep their identity (`List` diffing by `result.id`), so they don't re-layout.

**Selection:** after a refresh, keep `selected` if that ID is still in the results. Fall back to the first row only when the selection disappeared or the query text changed. Keep the scroll position too.

**In progress:** show nothing for queries that finish in under 300 ms. If a query runs longer, show a `ProgressView().controlSize(.small)` to the left of the "N results" caption. Keep the old count until the new one is ready. No spinner in the field, no shimmer.

**No Results:** keep `ContentUnavailableView.search(text:)` (system "No Results for '…'") and the existing "Search All Documents" button when scoped. It's shown only after a query completes, never during the debounce.

**Count:** caption copy is "1 result" / "N results", using `formatted()` (fix today's "1 results"). Post the VoiceOver announcement only when the count or query changed, never on idle refreshes. Otherwise a loop spams VoiceOver.

**Out of scope:** ranking, snippet content, panel layout, ⌘F Find.

title: #4 Three-pane library shell
description:
**Roadmap #:** 4 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
The app cannot navigate a library yet.

### Proposed behavior
Library root chooser, folder outline, direct-child document list, selection plumbing, read-only document placeholder; keyboard tree navigation; clear empty and error states. Usable shell before editor integration.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Category sidebar, document list, editor area layout.

### Likely files
Sources/Silkweb/SilkwebApp.swift, LibraryWorkspace.swift, FolderSidebar.swift, DocumentList.swift.

### Constraints
Thin app layer; scan via Core APIs from #1.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.4 Three-pane library shell
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§3 layout, §4 tokens, §5.1 empty states, §6 shortcuts). This ticket establishes the window that every later ticket plugs into, so build the structure exactly as specified even where later tickets fill it in.

### Entry points
- **First launch / no library** shows a Welcome view filling the whole window (no split view):
```
                 [books.vertical, 48pt, secondary]
                        Silkweb                    (.largeTitle)
           Write Markdown in folders you own.      (.title3, secondary)

   ┌──────────────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
   │ [folder]  Open Folder in Place… │  │ [plus.rectangle.on.folder] New Library… │
   │ Use an existing folder of     │  │ Start an empty library in a   │
   │ Markdown files where it is.   │  │ new folder.                   │
   └──────────────────────────────┘  └──────────────────────────────┘
        To copy files in instead, use File › Import Folder Copy…   (.caption, tertiary)
```
  The two cards are large bordered buttons, 240×88, 16pt gap. "Open Folder in Place…" is the default (Return). The Tab key moves between them. This is an owner decision: both are offered, and Import Copy is in the File menu only (enabled once a library is open).
- **File ▸ Open Folder in Place… ⌘O**: `NSOpenPanel`, directories only, prompt "Open", message "Choose a folder to use as your Silkweb library. Documents stay where they are."
- **File ▸ New Library… ⌥⌘N**: `NSSavePanel`, prompt "Create", default name "Silkweb Library" in ~/Documents. Creates the directory and opens it.
- Silkweb remembers the last library (security-scoped bookmark) and reopens it on launch. One library per window. Multiple libraries are out of scope.

### Layout (when a library is open)
`NavigationSplitView` with widths per §3. Sidebar = `NSOutlineView` source list:
1. Section header **LIBRARY**.
2. **All Documents** (`doc.on.doc`): virtual. Lists every document recursively.
3. **Library root** row (`books.vertical`, directory name), expanded by default. Its children are the folders (`folder`), in natural order (`localizedStandardCompare`).
Content column: direct-child documents of the selected folder. Row = title (`.headline`, 1 line) + second line `.subheadline` secondary: modified date + first line of text, truncated. Row height about 44pt. Detail: read-only document text placeholder for now (1.5 replaces it). Use a plain selectable `Text` in the system body font, inside a scroll view with the §4 editor insets.

### States
| Where | State | Display |
|---|---|---|
| Sidebar | loading > 300 ms | small `ProgressView` + "Loading library…" in place of the tree; after 1 s append the count ("… 4,210 documents") |
| List | folder has no docs | `ContentUnavailableView`: `doc.text`, "No Documents", "This folder is empty." (1.6 adds a "New Document" button) |
| List | whole library empty | "No Documents Yet", "Create a document or folder to get started." |
| List | All Documents / nothing selected | nothing selected → "Select a Folder" |
| Detail | no selection | `doc.text`, "No Document Selected", "Select a document in the list." |
| Detail | multi-selection | `doc.on.doc`, "3 Documents Selected" (no actions yet) |
| Window | root missing | full-window `ContentUnavailableView`: `externaldrive.badge.questionmark`, "Library Not Found", "Silkweb can’t find “<name>”. It may have been moved, renamed, or be on a disconnected drive." Buttons: **Locate…** (open panel) and **Open Another Folder…** |
| Window | permission denied | `lock`, "Can’t Open Library", "Silkweb doesn’t have permission to read “<name>”." Button: **Choose Folder Again…** |

Never crash or show a blank window. An empty folder still shows in the tree.

### Keyboard
- In the sidebar: ↑/↓ move selection. → expands, or moves to the first child if already expanded. ← collapses, or moves to the parent. ⌥→/⌥← expand/collapse all descendants. Type-select by name.
- Tab / ⇧Tab cycles focus sidebar → list → detail. **Go ▸ Folders ⌥⌘1 / Documents ⌥⌘2 / Editor ⌥⌘3** jump focus directly. Add a **Go** menu between View and Window.
- In the list: ↑/↓, ⇧-extend, ⌘A select all. Return is reserved for Rename (1.6).
- Selection and expansion state persist per library (tolerant JSON). 1.26 later adds tabs to the session.

### Window chrome
- Title = selected document name, or else the folder name. `navigationSubtitle` = folder path relative to the library (`Writing › Drafts`).
- View menu includes the system sidebar toggle ⌃⌘S and toolbar ⌥⌘T.
- No custom toolbar items yet. 1.6, 1.9, 1.18 and 1.20 add them in the positions their notes specify.

### Accessibility
Sidebar rows: label "<name>, folder" (root: "<name>, library"; All Documents: "All Documents"). List rows read as one element: "<title>, modified <relative date>". Welcome cards are buttons whose label is the title and whose hint is the subtitle.

### Out of scope
Create/rename (1.6), drag and drop (1.7), counts and sorting (1.9; until then, list order is name A→Z), editing (1.5), tags section (1.21), multiple windows/libraries.

**Boundary vs silkweb-1.39:** **1.40 owns the preview pipeline** — loading HTML and local assets in `WKWebView`, link policy, and **not scheduling preview re-renders while the preview pane is hidden** (fixes the idle 250 ms loop noted in silkweb-1.18 QA). **1.39 owns editor chrome only** — stable "Start writing…" placeholder drawing and bounded editor redraws; it verifies idle behavior after this ticket lands (do not re-open preview scheduling in 1.39 except to assert regressions).

**Boundary vs silkweb-1.18:** 1.18 delivered pane modes, outline navigation, and debounced rendering; this ticket fixes the **read-access root bug** and adds orchestrator-required real-WebKit tests. Close 1.18 after 1.40 + owner confirmation (orchestrator note).

Root cause (orchestrator, from code): `PreviewView.Coordinator.load()` writes the page HTML to `FileManager.temporaryDirectory/SilkwebPreview-<UUID>/<UUID>.html` (`PreviewView.swift:61,95`) and then calls `web.loadFileURL(file, allowingReadAccessTo: root)` with `root` = the LIBRARY folder (`:106`). WebKit only loads a file URL that is inside `readAccessURL`, so the page itself is refused → blank preview, and no images. silkweb-1.18 QA could not run WebKit in the sandbox, so this was never observed.

Fix (engineer decides, preferred first):
1. Serve the preview through a custom `WKURLSchemeHandler` (e.g. `silkweb-preview://page/<id>` for the HTML and `silkweb-preview://asset/<relative path>` for images), resolving asset paths strictly inside the library root (reuse the 1.16 containment rules), with correct MIME types. No temp files, no broad file access, works for read-only libraries. Update `HTMLRenderer`/`PreviewCoordinator` so image `src` uses the scheme, and update the CSP (`img-src silkweb-preview:`) and content rule list accordingly. Links: `#anchor` scroll, relative `.md` → open document, `https` → open in default browser (`decidePolicyFor`).
2. Acceptable alternative: page file inside the library's `.silkweb/preview/` (scanner-ignored) with `allowingReadAccessTo: root`, plus a temp-dir fallback for read-only libraries with readAccess on a common ancestor — only if (1) proves infeasible; explain why.

Keep JS disabled for page content, no network requests, debounced latest-result rendering.

**REQUIRED test — real WebKit, not code review:** an app test that creates a temp library with a document containing a heading, a paragraph, a table and `![p](img/p.png)` (a real 4×4 PNG written by the test), hosts the REAL `PreviewView`/`WKWebView` in an offscreen `NSWindow`, waits for navigation `didFinish` (timeout 10 s), then uses `web.evaluateJavaScript` (host-injected JS is allowed even with page JS disabled) to assert: `document.querySelector('h1').textContent` matches, the table exists, and `document.images[0].complete && document.images[0].naturalWidth == 4`. Also assert a remote `https` image is NOT loaded. If WebKit cannot run in the engineer/QA sandbox, the test must `XCTSkip` there with a clear message — the ORCHESTRATOR will run it unsandboxed and will verify it fails on 47cda03 and passes with the fix.

**Snapshot (silkweb-1.42):** after fix, `preview-mode` and `split-mode` scenarios should show non-blank rendered content when run outside the sandbox (QA views `preview-mode-light/dark.png`).

## UX notes — silkweb-1.40 Preview renders text and images
Foundation: `docs/design-system.md` §4 and §5.2 (Editor Banner), plus the 1.18 notes (preview.css, link rules). This is a bug fix. Everything from 1.18 stays as designed. These notes cover only the user-visible loading, error and image states.

### Loading
- Don't show a white flash, in dark mode especially. Keep `underPageBackgroundColor = .textBackgroundColor`. The pane shows a plain text-background color until the first `didFinish`.
- If the first render of a document takes **more than 400 ms**, show a centered small `ProgressView()` (indeterminate, no text) in the preview pane, and remove it on `didFinish`. Later re-renders while typing never show a spinner. The old content stays until the new one is ready (latest result only), and the scroll position is preserved (1.18).

### Error
- When navigation fails (`didFail` / `didFailProvisionalNavigation`, ignoring cancel), show a strip at the **top of the preview pane**, styled like the Editor Banner (§5.2: `.bar`, min 36pt, 12pt horizontal padding, `.controlSize(.small)`):
  `exclamationmark.triangle.fill` (systemOrange) · **"Preview couldn’t load."** (`.callout`) · reason on a second line (`.subheadline`, secondary; the `localizedDescription`) · trailing **Try Again** button.
- Put it inside the preview pane, not the editor's banner slot, so editor banners (save, conflict) keep priority. In Split mode it spans only the preview half.
- The strip clears on the next successful `didFinish`. Post an accessibility announcement once per failure, not once per retry.
- Today `preview.error` holds "Preview couldn’t load: <reason>". Split it into title + reason as above.

### Images in Preview
- Local image inside the library: rendered with `max-width: 100%` (1.18).
- **Missing local file** (resolves inside the root but doesn't exist): new `.sw-missing-image` box, styled like `.sw-remote-image` (1px dashed separator, 8px padding, secondary label). Copy: **"Missing image: <relative path>"**. 1.41 uses the same wording in the editor.
- Path outside the library root: the same box with **"Image outside library: <alt>"**.
- Remote `https` image: unchanged, **"Remote image not loaded: <alt>"**. Never fetched.

### Links (feedback only)
`#anchor` scrolls smoothly (instantly with Reduce Motion). Relative `.md` opens the document like a list selection. `https` opens the default browser. A link to a nonexistent or out-of-library document does nothing and calls `NSSound.beep()`. No alert.

### Out of scope
Scroll sync, find in preview, remote image loading, a preview theme change.

title: Show images inline in the Markdown editor
description:
Product owner (2026-10-01): like MWeb, images should appear inline inside the Markdown editor, not only in Preview. Moved into v1 from silkweb-2.23 (which keeps thumbnail/overlay/hidden display modes for v2).

**Boundary vs silkweb-2.23:** **1.41 delivers default inline display** (image drawn below the source line). **2.23** adds alternate modes and optional width metadata — depends on 1.41; do not scope modes here.

**Boundary vs silkweb-1.15 / 1.43:** Insertion and storage paths are owned by 1.15/1.43; this ticket only **renders** resolved local paths. Remote URLs are never fetched (align with 1.16/1.18 policy).

Behavior: for every line that is (or contains) a local image reference `![alt](relative/path)` that resolves inside the library root, keep the Markdown source line fully visible and editable, and draw the image directly **below** that line in the editor, scaled to fit the text column width (max natural size, keep aspect ratio, cap height to ~70% of the viewport). The image is not part of the text (no attachment characters inserted into the `.md`; on-disk Markdown never changes). Caret/selection/undo/IME behave as if the image weren't there; arrow keys move between text lines normally. Remote (`https`) images are NOT fetched — show a small "Remote image" placeholder chip instead. Missing files show a "Missing image" placeholder. Clicking the image selects the source line; double-click opens the image in Quick Look/Preview.app (or Reveal in Finder). Animated GIFs may show first frame.

Implementation notes: use TextKit (`NSTextLayoutManager` / `NSTextLayoutFragment` custom view providers, or extra line-fragment spacing + overlay image views positioned from layout) — engineer decides; images decoded and downsampled off the main thread (ImageIO thumbnail at column width × backing scale), cached by path+mtime, invalidated when the file or column width changes. No per-keystroke work beyond affected paragraphs (`AGENTS.md` performance rules). Reuse asset path resolution/containment from silkweb-1.15/1.16/1.40/1.43. Must not regress silkweb-1.29 layout recursion fix or silkweb-1.39 idle-redraw fix.

**REQUIRED tests:** Core tests for image-reference detection per paragraph (multiple images, alt with brackets, percent-encoded paths, outside-root rejected, remote vs local). Offscreen app test hosting the real editor with a document containing a real 40×20 PNG: assert an inline image view/fragment is laid out under the image line with width ≤ column width and correct aspect ratio; resize sweep keeps it fitted; typing before/after the image line keeps the string unchanged except the typed text; saved file contents unchanged by display.

**Snapshot (silkweb-1.42):** scenario `editor-image` should show inline image below the syntax line (QA views `editor-image-light/dark.png`).
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.41 Inline images in the editor
Foundation: `docs/design-system.md` §4 (editor typography: 720pt column, 40pt inset, semantic colors), plus 1.15 (insertion), 1.40 (placeholder copy) and 1.43 (`media/` paths). The design is original: the Markdown source line stays visible and the picture sits directly beneath it, like a figure under its caption.

### Layout
```
  ![Kettle on the scale](media/3F2…/kettle.png)      ← source line, normal Markdown styling (1.12 styler)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐      ← 6pt gap above
  │                 image                    │      fitted to the text column, radius 4pt
  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘      ← 10pt gap below, then the next line
  Next paragraph…
```
- **Width:** min(natural width in points, text column width). The column is the editor's content width: max 720pt minus insets, the same edge the text wraps at. Never upscale, so a 40×20 image stays 40×20. Left-aligned with the text, not centered. A small image floating in the middle of a writing column looks orphaned.
- **Height:** keep the aspect ratio, capped at **70% of the visible viewport height**. If the cap applies, the width shrinks proportionally.
- Corner radius 4pt and clipped. No border and no shadow. Images are never inverted or tinted in dark mode. Transparent PNGs show the `textBackgroundColor` behind them.
- Several images in one paragraph: stack them in source order, 8pt apart, all under that paragraph's last line.
- Don't render images for `![…]()` inside code spans or fenced/indented code blocks, or for escaped `\![`. Use the Core detection the ticket asks for.
- The reserved space must be **exactly** the final display height. Read pixel dimensions from the file header (ImageIO properties, off-main) before reserving, so the text never jumps when decoding finishes.

### States (all inside the same reserved slot, left-aligned)
| State | Visual |
|---|---|
| **Loading** (dimensions known, bitmap decoding) | Rounded 4pt rect at final size, filled with `quaternarySystemFill`. No spinner. The image fades in over 120 ms when ready (instantly with Reduce Motion) |
| **Remote** (`http(s)`) | **Chip**: height 28pt, horizontal padding 10pt, radius 6pt, `quaternarySystemFill`. SF Symbol `photo` 12pt secondary, then `.callout` secondary text **"Remote image not loaded"**. Never fetched |
| **Missing** (inside root, file absent) | The same chip with symbol `exclamationmark.triangle` (secondary, **not** orange; it's informational) and **"Missing image: kettle.png"** (last path component, middle-truncated to the column) |
| **Outside library** | The same chip, `photo` symbol, **"Image outside library"** |
| **Unreadable / not an image** | The same chip, `exclamationmark.triangle`, **"Can’t display image"** |

Placeholder copy matches the Preview wording in 1.40, so both surfaces say the same thing. Chips use the semantic fill and secondary label, which reads correctly in light and dark.

### Interaction
- **Hover:** the pointer stays an I-beam over text and becomes an arrow over the image/chip. No hover effects.
- **Click** the image or chip: selects the whole source line, excluding the newline. This is an ordinary text selection, so ⌫ deletes the reference and ⌘Z restores it. While the source line is fully selected, draw a 2pt `controlAccentColor` ring (inset, radius 4pt) around the image. That makes the link between text and picture visible.
- **Double-click** the image: opens it in **Quick Look** (`QLPreviewPanel`, orchestrator default). Space or Escape closes it, and focus returns to the editor with the selection intact. Double-clicking a chip does nothing (beep).
- **Context menu** on the image (text-only per §4): **Quick Look**, **Reveal in Finder**, **Copy Image**. Chips: **Copy Path** only.
- Caret, arrows, ⌥/⌘ arrows, selection drags, IME and undo treat the image as absent: ↓ from the source line goes to the next text line. Dragging the image does nothing in v1. File drops onto the image go to the nearest text insertion point (1.15).
- Edits: when the path text changes, the slot updates after the editor's normal debounce. A valid → invalid change swaps to the chip without changing height until the new state is known, which avoids flicker.
- Focus Mode (1.27): images in dimmed paragraphs take the same dim alpha as their text.

### Performance feel
Typing never waits on images. Decode at column width × backing scale. A window resize re-fits immediately using the cached bitmap (scaled), then re-decodes after the resize ends if the width grew by more than 25%.

### Accessibility
Each image is an `NSAccessibility` image element after its line: label = alt text, or "Image, kettle.png" when the alt is empty; help "Double-click to open in Quick Look". Chips use their visible copy as the label. VoiceOver reading the text is unaffected, since the source line is still read.

### Snapshot
`editor-image` (1.42): the 400×240 fixture is shown left-aligned under its `![…](…)` line at natural size, or fitted if the column is narrower, in both light and dark. Suggest adding a second line with a remote URL to the fixture so the chip shows too.

### Consistency / out of scope
Same placeholder vocabulary as 1.40 Preview. Same paths as 1.43. Out of scope (2.23): thumbnail/hidden/overlay modes, width syntax, resizing handles, drag-to-reorder, animated GIF playback (first frame only), PDF page previews.

title: Offscreen screenshot harness so QA can visually verify the real UI
description:
Product owner request: QA must visually verify UI changes, without ever touching the owner's desktop (no app launch on screen, no GUI automation).

**Boundary:** This ticket is **QA infrastructure only** — it does not fix preview (silkweb-1.40), editor placeholder flicker (silkweb-1.39), or outline styling (silkweb-1.44). It hosts real views offscreen and writes PNGs so later UI tickets can add snapshot scenarios.

Build a snapshot tool that renders the REAL Silkweb views offscreen and writes PNGs:
- New SwiftPM executable target `SilkwebSnapshot` (depends on the Silkweb app module via a small shared library target if needed, or move testable UI into a `SilkwebUI` library target used by both the app and the tool — engineer decides; keep the app target thin) OR an XCTest-based snapshot suite — must be runnable as: `./scripts/snapshot.sh <out-dir> [scenario ...]`
- It copies a fixture library (`Test_Library` → temp dir, never modifying `Test_Library`) plus a generated 400×240 PNG image fixture, builds the real `LibraryWorkspace` + split/window content in an `NSWindow` that is NEVER ordered front (no Dock icon, `NSApplication.setActivationPolicy(.prohibited)`), sizes it (default 1400×900), lays it out, drives app state programmatically (select folder/document, set pane mode, open Inspector, begin rename, open Quick Open, etc.), waits for async work (scan, preview navigation `didFinish`) with timeouts, and captures via `NSView.cacheDisplay(in:to:)` — and for `WKWebView` content, `WKWebView.takeSnapshot` composited into the window image.
- Each scenario renders in BOTH light and dark appearance: `<out-dir>/<scenario>-light.png` / `-dark.png`, plus `<out-dir>/manifest.json` listing scenarios, sizes, and any errors/timeouts (a scenario that times out must be reported, never silently skipped).
- Initial scenarios: `library-overview` (All Documents), `folder-selected` (Coffee/Brewing Guides), `editor-document` (Pour-Over in Five Steps), `editor-image` (doc with the image fixture), `preview-mode`, `split-mode`, `inspector-outline`, `rename-active`, `quick-open`, `search-results`, `empty-document` (placeholder), `read-only-banner`. Scenario list is data-driven so later tickets add scenarios easily.
- Must work outside the agent sandbox (the orchestrator runs it); inside the sandbox it should still run the non-WebKit scenarios and clearly mark WebKit ones as `unavailable in this environment`.
- Document usage in `AGENTS.md` (Build & Test section).

**REQUIRED tests:** a unit/integration test that runs two scenarios into a temp dir and asserts PNGs exist, are the expected pixel size (respecting backing scale), are not blank (pixel variance above a threshold), and dark ≠ light.

**Suggested build order (v1 image/preview batch):** silkweb-1.26 → **1.42** → 1.40 → 1.44 → 1.43 → 1.39 → 1.41.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.42 Offscreen snapshot harness (QA only)
There's no user-facing UI. These notes define what each scenario must visibly show, so QA has a clear eyeball checklist. All scenarios use a 1400×900 window and the default column widths (§3): sidebar 220, list 300, inspector 240 when shown. Single tab unless stated (orchestrator). Fixture documents come from the temp copy of `Test_Library`.

| Scenario | Drive state | Must visibly show |
|---|---|---|
| `library-overview` | Select **All Documents** | Sidebar with LIBRARY section, All Documents selected with its count, root folder row; full document list; editor shows the first document or the empty detail state |
| `folder-selected` | Select `Coffee › Brewing Guides` | Folder row selected and expanded path; list limited to that folder; content subtitle "N documents" |
| `editor-document` | Open "Pour-Over in Five Steps", Editor mode | Styled Markdown (headings, lists) in the centered 720pt column; window title = document name |
| `editor-image` | Open the image fixture doc | 400×240 image under its source line (1.41) |
| `preview-mode` | Same doc, Preview mode | Rendered HTML with heading/body text, **not blank** (1.40) |
| `split-mode` | Split mode | Editor left and rendered preview right, 50/50 |
| `inspector-outline` | Show Outline (⌘7) | Inspector with "Outline" header and heading rows; current-heading bar |
| `outline-hierarchy` *(added by 1.44)* | H1–H6 fixture, caret in the H3 | Graduated sizes and indentation; H3 row highlighted |
| `rename-active` | Begin rename on a list row | Inline Rename Field with the base name selected (§5.3) |
| `quick-open` | Open Quick Open, type "brew" | Panel with `.title3` field and filtered results |
| `search-results` | Search Library for "coffee" | Results with matches highlighted |
| `empty-document` | New empty document, editor focused | Steady "Start writing…" in tertiary color (1.39) |
| `read-only-banner` | Read-only fixture document | Editor Banner with `info.circle` and read-only message |
| `tabs-open` *(after 1.26)* | 3 documents in tabs, middle active | Tab bar with three tabs, active one distinct |

### Rendering rules
- Each scenario is rendered twice, with `NSAppearance` `.aqua` and `.darkAqua` set on the window. Dark must actually be dark everywhere, including the WebKit snapshot.
- The caret is captured in a deterministic state (hidden is fine), so blink timing doesn't vary between images.
- No hover or focus-ring artifacts except where the scenario is about focus (rename field).

### Manifest status values (exact strings)
`ok`, `timeout`, `error: <message>`, `unavailable in this environment` (WebKit inside the sandbox). Report the pixel size and backing scale for each PNG.

### Out of scope

title: Store copied images in a visible media/ folder (like MWeb) and migrate .silkweb-assets
description:
Product owner decision (2026-10-01): copied images/attachments must live in a **visible** folder so they show in Finder — `<Library root>/media/<document-id>/<file>` (MWeb-style), replacing the hidden `<root>/.silkweb-assets/<document-id>/` used by silkweb-1.15 (`AssetStore.swift:52`). Still copy (never link to the original), still one central location so moving notes never breaks images, still relative links.

**Boundary vs silkweb-1.15:** 1.15 behavior (paste/drop/Format ▸ Image…, collision names, undo text-only) is unchanged except **storage path and scanner treatment**. Preview (1.40) and inline editor display (1.41) must resolve both legacy `.silkweb-assets/` and new `media/` paths until migration completes.

**Boundary vs silkweb-1.41:** 1.43 lands **before** 1.41 in the build batch so new inserts use `media/`; 1.41 adds drawing below image lines, not asset storage.

Requirements:
1. `AssetStore` writes to `media/<document-id>/` (same collision/percent-encoding rules). Mark the folder as Silkweb's with a small marker file (e.g. `media/.silkweb-media`) so Silkweb can tell it apart from a user's own folder named `media`. If the root already has a user `media` folder WITHOUT the marker that contains `.md` documents, don't take it over: use `Media Assets/` (marked) instead and say so in the report.
2. Sidebar/library: the marked media folder is NOT shown as a library folder in the sidebar, its files never appear as documents, counts exclude it; Import Copy (1.10), Trash (1.8), moves (1.7), reconcile (1.11), search index (1.19) and the move-link rewriter all treat it as the asset store (no "unmanaged" surprises; links into it are rewritten correctly when notes move).
3. Migration on library open: if `.silkweb-assets/` exists, move its contents into `media/` (atomic per file, no overwrite — collision → unique name), rewrite every document link that pointed into `.silkweb-assets` to the new path (reuse 1.7 rewrite machinery, dirty buffers saved first), remove the empty old folder, and record a versioned metadata flag so it runs once. Must be crash-safe/idempotent (resume after interruption) and leave both old and new paths resolvable until links are rewritten.
4. Preview (1.40) and inline editor images (1.41) resolve `media/` paths (this ticket updates Core path resolution shared by preview and editor).

**REQUIRED tests:** Core tests for new location + marker, user-owned `media` conflict, sidebar/scan exclusion, migration (links rewritten, files moved, idempotent re-run, interrupted mid-way then resumed), and that moving a note keeps media links valid.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.43 Visible `media/` folder and migration
Foundation: `docs/design-system.md` §2 (vocabulary, curly quotes), §5.2 (banner styling), §5.5 (alerts); 1.15 (insertion, which is unchanged). The goal is for images to be **boringly visible in Finder** while staying invisible as clutter inside Silkweb.

### What the user sees
- **Finder:** `My Library/media/<document-id>/kettle.png`. The folder is lowercase `media`. The marker `.silkweb-media` is a dot-file, so Finder hides it.
- **Silkweb sidebar / document list / counts / search / Quick Open / Move To… picker / import destination picker:** the marked folder never appears. It's the library's asset store, not a Folder (§2 vocabulary: never call it a "Folder" in UI copy; say "the “media” folder" only in Finder-facing messages).
- **Inserted Markdown:** `![kettle](../media/3F2…/kettle.png)`, relative and readable (1.15 encoding rules).
- **Fallback:** if a user-owned `media/` with `.md` documents exists, the store is `Media Assets/` (marked; orchestrator: accepted long-term). It also stays hidden in the sidebar. The user's own `media` folder remains a normal Folder. All copy below substitutes the actual folder name.
- A user `media/` **without** `.md` documents and without a marker is adopted (the marker is added). *Consequence: if it was visible in the sidebar before (as an empty or images-only Folder), it disappears from the sidebar.* That's acceptable because it holds no documents. Mention it in the report.

### Migration feedback (runs on library open)
- **Fast path (< 1 s):** silent. No banner, no alert. Links simply point to `media/`.
- **Longer:** a library-level strip at the top of the detail column, styled like the Editor Banner (§5.2: `.bar`, 36pt, 12pt padding, `.small`), below the tab bar and above document banners:
  `info.circle` (secondary) · **"Moving images to the “media” folder…"** · trailing small determinate `ProgressView` (files done / total) at 120pt wide. No Cancel. The operation is resumable and safe to quit mid-way.
  The strip only appears if the migration is still running after 1 s, so it never flashes. It disappears on completion. No success message.
- The UI stays usable during migration. A document whose links are being rewritten follows 1.7 behavior: it's saved first if dirty, the rewrite applies to the open buffer, and the editor shows the updated path text. **The rewrite is not on the user's undo stack** (same as move-link rewrites).
- **Partial failure** (unreadable or locked files): the same strip with `exclamationmark.triangle.fill` (systemOrange) · **"Some images couldn’t be moved to the “media” folder."** · second line (`.subheadline`, secondary) **"Their links still work. Silkweb will try again next time this library opens."** · buttons **Details** (popover list "kettle.png — reason", same as 1.15's AssetErrorBanner) and **Try Again**, plus a close ✕ ("Dismiss message").
- **Read-only library:** don't migrate. Keep resolving `.silkweb-assets/` silently, with no banner.
- Post an accessibility announcement for the failure strip only.

### Interactions elsewhere
- Move to Trash on a document does **not** delete its media (1.15: no implicit asset deletion).
- Moving documents (1.7) never moves media. Links are rewritten so they stay valid.
- Reveal in Finder for an image comes from 1.41's image context menu. No new menu items here.

### Out of scope
Asset cleanup or garbage collection, a Media browser UI (v2 2.34), renaming the media folder from Silkweb, settings to choose its name.

New inserts use a visible, marked media/<document-id>/ store. A user-owned media directory with Markdown anywhere beneath it is preserved; Media Assets is the accepted fallback.
